svg.title: Halting a bad desktop update and rolling forward
svg.desc: Each bar shows all stable-channel installs of TaskFlow Desktop. Ticks mark the 1.9.1 rollout at 1, 5, and 20 percent. Day 2: crash-free sessions fell, so 1.9.1 is halted with 20 percent of installs on 1.9.1 and 80 percent still on 1.9.0. Day 3: the fix 1.9.2 starts; every install on 1.9.1 gets it at once, plus 5 percent of the rest, while the remaining 1.9.0 installs wait for their bucket. Day 4: rule 2 reaches 25 percent of the rest. Day 6: rule 2 reaches 100 percent and 1.9.2 is on every install. The update server's rules for 1.9.2: rule 1, evaluated first, offers 1.9.2 to 100 percent of installs whose current version is 1.9.1, because they already have the bug; rule 2 offers it to older versions when the bucket, the hash of the install ID plus 1.9.2 modulo 10000, is below the percentage times 100. You cannot uninstall a bad version, but you can replace it first where it landed.

g.text: Halt a bad update, then roll forward: fix the affected installs first
Rules on the update server for 1.9.2
Rule 1 (first): current version is 1.9.1 -> offer 1.9.2 to 100% now; these installs already have the bug.
Rule 2: older versions -> bucket = hash(install ID + "1.9.2") mod 10000; offer when bucket < percent x 100.
You cannot uninstall a bad version, but you can replace it first where it landed.
